identity.title: Localized LLQ tenderness (with prior diverticulitis episode history)

technique.how: Palpate all four quadrants starting away from the pain; record whether direct tenderness is confined to the left lower quadrant, whether there is guarding, rebound or a palpable mass, and ask specifically about prior confirmed diverticulitis episodes and about vomiting.
technique.prerequisites: Supine, knees slightly flexed, abdomen exposed; analgesia does not need to be withheld.

interpretation.positive_finding: Tenderness confined to the LLQ, especially with a prior episode, absence of vomiting and raised CRP, makes acute diverticulitis likely (97% PPV for the three-feature rule in Lameris' ED cohort).
interpretation.negative_finding: Diffuse or right-sided tenderness argues against uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulitis but not against right-sided diverticulitis (common in Asian patients) or complicated disease; clinical diagnosis alone misses a substantial share of cases.
interpretation.pitfalls: Clinical diagnosis of diverticulitis has a PPV of only 0.65 in unselected ED abdominal pain; redundant sigmoid, appendicitis, gynaecological disease and colon cancer mimic it. Peritonism, mass or systemic toxicity suggest abscess or perforation and need CT.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: diverticulitis leads the differential; CT if fever, peritonism, mass, immunosuppression or first episode. Negative: widen differential and image.

estimates.target_condition: COMPOSITE: direct tenderness only in LLQ AND no vomiting AND CRP >50 mg/L (acute diverticulitis)
estimates.population: 126 ED patients with clinically suspected diverticulitis (from 1,021 with acute abdominal pain); 80 had final diagnosis of diverticulitis
estimates.reference_standard: final diagnosis after imaging and follow-up (expert panel)
estimates.computed_from: 2x2 from abstract: 30 with all 3 features, 29 diverticulitis (TP=29, FP=1); of 96 without all 3 features, 45 did not have diverticulitis (TN=45, FN=51). Sens 29/80=0.363; spec 45/46=0.978; LR+ 16.7; LR- 0.65; prevalence 80/126=0.635
estimates.quote: 30 patients had all 3 features (24%), of whom 29 had a final diagnosis of acute diverticulitis (97%; 95% CI: 83%-99%).

sources.citation: Laméris W, van Randen A, van Gulik TM, Busch OR, Winkelhagen J, Bossuyt PM, Stoker J, Boermeester MA. A clinical decision rule to establish the diagnosis of acute diverticulitis at the emergency department. Dis Colon Rectum. 2010.
Andeweg CS, Knobben L, Hendriks JC, Bleichrodt RP, van Goor H. How to diagnose acute left-sided colonic diverticulitis: proposal for a clinical scoring system. Ann Surg. 2011.
Toorenvliet BR, Bakker RF, Breslau PJ, Merkus JW, Hamming JF. Colonic diverticulitis: a prospective analysis of diagnostic accuracy and clinical decision-making. Colorectal Dis. 2010.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not rely on a clinical diagnosis without imaging in immunosuppressed, elderly frail, or first-episode patients, or when peritonism, mass or sepsis is present.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Generalized peritonitis, hemodynamic instability or a tender mass suggests perforation or abscess: urgent CT and surgical review.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Location-of-tenderness recording was by the treating ED clinician before imaging in Lameris; no kappa reported in abstracts seen.

extraction_notes: Status set to partially_quantified deliberately: the only numeric estimate is a COMPOSITE rule (LLQ-only tenderness + no vomiting + CRP >50) computed from the abstract 2x2; LLQ tenderness alone has no accessible sens/spec (Lameris Table with univariate features not viewable; not in PMC). Andeweg 2011 (287 ED patients, ALCD prevalence 43%) identifies 'localization of abdominal tenderness in the lower left abdomen' and '1 or more previous episodes' as independent predictors but gives no per-feature accuracy in the abstract. Toorenvliet 2010: 'The positive and negative predictive values for the clinical diagnosis of colonic diverticulitis were 0.65 and 0.98 respectively' (Abstract) in 802 consecutive ED abdominal-pain patients (57 diverticulitis) - this is clinical gestalt, not the sign, so not entered as an estimate. Title mentions prior-episode history, but no diagnostic-accuracy number for that history element was found.
